diagnostics.message: `:resource.aws_cloudwatch_event_target.dispatcher` registers the dispatcher Lambda as an EventBridge target, but nothing orders it after `:resource.aws_lambda_permission.allow_cloudwatch_to_call_lambda`. The target is a separate resource from the rule, so the dispatcher can be wired to the bus before the resource-based policy allowing `events.amazonaws.com` to invoke it exists — any `workflow_job` event arriving in that window is dropped with an access-denied error. The AWS provider docs for `aws_cloudwatch_event_target` explicitly call out that a Lambda target requires `aws_lambda_permission` to be in place.

`:resource.aws_lambda_function.webhook` only references the webhook role ARN (`aws_iam_role.webhook_lambda.arn`), so it is not ordered after `:resource.aws_iam_role_policy.webhook_logging`. The function can be created and invoked (via API Gateway) while its execution role still lacks `logs:CreateLogGroup/CreateLogStream/PutLogEvents`, which makes the very first webhook invocations fail with CloudWatch Logs permission errors. Wiring the Lambda to its execution-role policies is the documented pattern for aws_lambda_function.

`:resource.aws_lambda_function.dispatcher` is not ordered after `:resource.aws_iam_role_policy.dispatcher_logging`, so the function and the EventBridge target can be live before the dispatcher role can write to CloudWatch Logs. The first `workflow_job` events handled by the dispatcher fail with logs permission errors until the policy catches up.

`:resource.aws_lambda_function.webhook` reads the GitHub App webhook secret/SSM parameters at cold start (PARAMETER_GITHUB_APP_WEBHOOK_SECRET), but has no dependency on `:resource.aws_iam_role_policy.webhook_ssm`. The function can be invoked before its role can `ssm:GetParameter*`, causing the first webhook deliveries to fail authentication.

`:resource.aws_lambda_function.webhook` decrypts SecureString SSM parameters / encrypted environment variables, but is not ordered after `:resource.aws_iam_role_policy.webhook_kms`. Without the KMS policy attached first, invocations that touch the customer-managed key fail with KMS access-denied errors.

`:resource.aws_lambda_function.webhook` publishes to the custom event bus on every accepted GitHub event, but is not ordered after `:resource.aws_iam_role_policy.webhook_eventbridge`. A webhook that arrives before the policy is attached cannot `events:PutEvents` and the job event is lost.

`:resource.aws_lambda_function.webhook` is configured with an active `tracing_config` block, but is not ordered after `:resource.aws_iam_role_policy.xray`, so the function can run before its role may call `xray:PutTraceSegments`/`PutTelemetryRecords`.

When the function runs inside a VPC, `:resource.aws_lambda_function.webhook` needs the `AWSLambdaVPCAccessExecutionRole` attachment to manage ENIs, but it has no dependency on `:resource.aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.webhook_vpc_execution_role`. The function can become invocable while the attachment is still pending, producing network/ENI permission failures on the first calls.

`:resource.aws_lambda_function.dispatcher` reads SSM runner-matcher config at cold start (PARAMETER_RUNNER_MATCHER_CONFIG_PATH/VERSION), but is not ordered after `:resource.aws_iam_role_policy.dispatcher_ssm`. Events handled before the policy attaches fail on the SSM lookup.

`:resource.aws_lambda_function.dispatcher` depends on `:resource.aws_iam_role_policy.dispatcher_sqs` for `sqs:SendMessage` to the job queues, but nothing orders the function after the policy. A `workflow_job` event consumed before the policy exists fails to enqueue and the job is lost.

`:resource.aws_lambda_function.dispatcher` needs KMS access (encrypted environment / SSM values) but is not ordered after `:resource.aws_iam_role_policy.dispatcher_kms`, so early invocations can fail with KMS access-denied errors.

`:resource.aws_lambda_function.dispatcher` has an active `tracing_config` block but is not ordered after `:resource.aws_iam_role_policy.dispatcher_xray`, so tracing calls from the first invocations fail because the execution role lacks the X-Ray permissions yet.

`:resource.aws_lambda_function.dispatcher` is a VPC-attached function (dynamic `vpc_config`) yet has no ordering on `:resource.aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.dispatcher_vpc_execution_role`. The function can be registered as an EventBridge target before the VPC access execution policy is attached, so the first dispatcher invocations fail on ENI permissions.
